A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DrivingGen and contain readable main text, references, and Appendices A and B.1-B.9. Their tables, figures, equations, and experimental content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 generative models in Table 3, SLAM pipeline experiments in Table 4, and human-preference validation in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, SLAM pipeline experiments, and human-preference validation in Tables 3-4 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The DrivingGen evaluation pipeline, trajectory reconstruction and failure handling, metric computations, and VLM disappearance assessment remain unchanged in Section 3.2 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both retain Internet-sourced open-domain scenarios and ego-conditioned data from Zod, DrivingDojo, COVLA, nuPlan, and WOMD. Weather, geographic, lighting, and maneuver coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 evaluates the same 14 models in each track, and Table 4 retains the same SLAM pipeline comparators. The removed Tongyi citation was related-work coverage, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both use 400 samples, 200 per track, and a 100-frame prediction horizon. Model sizes, evaluation metrics, the 20-video SLAM comparison, and human-validation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The failure-handling ablation and SLAM comparison in Appendix B.2, together with human-alignment analysis in Appendix B.9, are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the human-preference win ratios and Spearman correlations in Figure 5. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Result entries and rankings in Tables 3-4 and Figure 5 are unchanged. For example, Vista's ego-conditioned ADE remains 19.70, and the failure-handling pipeline retains 20/20 reconstruction success with ADE 16.84.

T1.justification: The FTD, MMP, trajectory-quality, and trajectory-consistency definitions and formulas in Appendix B remain identical. Citation corrections around MMP do not change its mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a diverse driving benchmark, driving-specific metrics, and evaluation of 14 models revealing visual-realism versus trajectory-fidelity trade-offs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model performance and SLAM-related measurement limitations are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same qualifications concerning sample coverage, open-loop evaluation, single-camera inputs, and untested forms of controllability.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation defaults, reconstruction details, VLM prompt, and hardware/runtime estimates. The project website and dataset/code release statement are unchanged; reference-URL edits concern bibliography metadata.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 and the bibliography remove the Tongyi/Wanxiang Video citation. Other edited references match existing works, including consolidated LTX-Video duplicates and the changed DriveDreamer-2 publication entry; substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and cleans citation and bibliography formatting, notably replacing malformed IEEE citations such as '996, 2022' and consolidating duplicate LTX-Video entries. Narrative wording and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: The running conference header and bibliography edits produce limited layout and text-reflow changes, including in Appendices A.1 and B.4. Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-5 retain their content, design, and captions.

improvement.justification: Corrected IEEE citations in Section 3.2.2 and Appendix B.4 and consolidated LTX-Video references improve attribution and bibliographic clarity. Some reference URLs are removed, slightly reducing lookup convenience, but the scientific evidence and technical documentation remain intact. The net improvement is limited to editorial quality.
